newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy reaffirms support for Polish NATO, EU bids.
newsitem.headline: Italy reaffirms support for Polish NATO, EU bids.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi on Tuesday reaffirmed Italy's support for Poland's entry into NATO and the European Union and said he did not think Russia would veto the eastward expansion of the military alliance.
"I would like to clarify once and for all that Italy's position is in favour," Prodi told a joint news conference after talks with visiting Polish President Aleksander Kwasniewski.
"I am convinced that there will not be a Russian veto, many positions have moved," he added, in response to a question.
Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic are expected to be invited to join the 16-member NATO at a summit in July in Spain in an eastward expansion that Russia firmly opposes.
Poland hopes to start negotiations on EU membership next year and to join some time after the year 2000.
Pope John Paul, himself a Pole, on Monday voiced his support for Polish entry into NATO and the EU.
Kwasniewski said that Italy, which has championed Romania and Slovenia's bids for early NATO membership, had also given its wholehearted support.
"There is no shadow of doubt over the Italian government's support for Poland's entry into NATO and the EU," he said.
